Subject: DPA: notification timing and forensic evidence access

Hi Jordan,

Quick note as we're going through the DPA with legal: can you confirm Redwood's maximum notification window for a confirmed data integrity or confidentiality incident affecting our data? FinexCorp's counsel is asking for definitive language around (1) when Redwood will notify, (2) what granularity of scope will be shared within the notification period, and (3) whether Redwood will provide live forensic access (read-only query access or evidence export) to our security team or an approved third-party investigator.

Also: Finex has strict cross-border transfer constraints for patient-related PII. If evidence must be preserved or transferred, what are your proposed controls and timelines?

If useful, we've attached FinexCorp's suggested evidence-handling requirements (for your reference). Looking to get a pragmatic path that avoids a 72-hour hard requirement if there are operational restraints, but we do need clear escalation and cooperation commitments.

Thanks,
Alyssa Moreno
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
FinexCorp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: DPA: notification timing and forensic evidence access

Alyssa / team — thanks for the clear asks. High-level responses below; Marissa and Ben are looped for legal/ops detail.

1) Notification window: Redwood commits to an initial notification within 48 hours of confirming a security incident that materially affects a customer’s data. The initial notice will state the suspected scope, impacted services, and immediate mitigation steps.

2) Scope granularity: Within that initial notice we provide a summary (systems, time range, approximate record counts). A more detailed scoped report (including object IDs and affected tenant slices) will follow within 7 business days where available and subject to forensic integrity.

3) Forensic access: Redwood supports provisioned, read-only forensic access to customers' data environments for approved third-party investigators or customer security teams, subject to a scoped MOU and controls. If live access is not possible due to multitenancy or sensitive backend artifacts, Redwood will provide verified exports and signed integrity manifests.

4) Cross-border/evidence transfer: We can preserve evidence in-region and provide encrypted exports to a nominated party. Transfers outside a region require the customer to accept an addendum that documents permitted transfers, or we can support on-site/export to customer-controlled storage.

Operational caveats: there are scenarios where an immediate 24-hour detailed handoff is not technically feasible (ongoing containment, active threat eradication, or when sharing would interfere with law enforcement). In those cases we'll escalate to a senior incident manager and provide a rolling update cadence.

Marissa: can you take point on drafting a proposed DPA clause (language + optional SLA exception template) and a brief forensic access MOU? Ben / Marcus — can you prepare the evidence-handling matrix and a recommended timeline for production/export options?

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Alyssa / team — draft language and operational artifacts attached for review. Key points in the draft DPA wording:

- InitialNotification: "Redwood will provide an initial written notification to Customer within forty-eight (48) hours after Redwood reasonably believes a Security Incident has materially affected Customer Data. The initial notice will include the incident date/time window, impacted services, and preliminary containment actions."

- DetailReport: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a detailed incident report (including affected object identifiers and estimated record counts) within seven (7) business days, subject to forensic integrity and any legal holds."

- ForensicAccess: "At Customer's request, Redwood will grant time-limited, role-based, read-only forensic access to Customer or Customer's designated investigator under a mutually agreed MOU that includes scope, allowed queries, and non-repudiation controls. If live access cannot be granted, Redwood will provide reproducible exported datasets with integrity checks and an audit log describing the extraction process."

- SLA Exception / Escalation: "If providing the DetailReport within seven (7) business days would materially impede incident remediation or law enforcement cooperation, Redwood may request an exception. Such request will be documented, justified, and approved by Redwood's Chief Security Officer or designee; Customer will be notified with an alternative delivery timeline."

Ben / Marcus — attached is a proposed evidence-handling matrix (forensic-access-matrix.xlsx) that maps likely request types to turnaround times and export formats. Also included is an evidence transfer flowchart (evidence-transfer-flowchart.png) for the DPA exhibit.

Alyssa — two asks: (1) please confirm whether Finex needs a hard 72-hour detailed delivery requirement or whether the 7 business day window with exception language is acceptable; (2) confirm the preferred method for exports (S3 to customer account, encrypted transfer to Finex bucket, or on-site handoff).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Jordan — appreciate the pragmatic approach and the attachments. FinexCorp can accept the 48-hour initial notice plus the 7 business day detailed report, provided the SLA exception clause includes a requirement to escalate to our legal liaison and provides weekly rolling updates until full delivery.

On exports: preferred path is encrypted S3 transfer into a FinexCorp-controlled bucket (cross-account), with an integrity manifest and a signed chain-of-custody statement. We'll send a short MOU template for the access window and investigator verification.

I'll loop in procurement next week to add the addendum language.
